newsitem.title: USA: AIDS activists protest drug cost at stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: AIDS activists protest drug cost at stock exchange.

text.p: More than 200 demonstraters protested the high cost of AIDS drugs near the New York Stock Exchange Monday and 55 were arrested, police said.
Most of those arrested would be charged with disorderly conduct, said police official Louis Anemone.

Anemone said most of those arrested sat down on the sidewalk and refused police orders to move. A handful of others were arrested for throwing an unidentified liquid at the stock exchange and one was arrested for allegedly kicking a police officer.
The stock exchange opened trading at its normal time but many workers in the area were delayed as police demanded identification from those attempting to enter several streets around the exchange.

The protesters, representing Act Up, a political activist group, chanted "Fight AIDS," and "Act Up," and carried placards saying "AIDS Drugs: Your Money or Your Life" as they marched down Broadway, slowing traffic.
An Act Up spokesman said the group chose the exchange as the site for their protest because it symbolised the heart of corporate America.
They were protesting against pharmaceutical companies, which they claim charge exorbitant prices for AIDS drugs.
NYSE Chairman Richard Grasso came out of the exchange briefly around the time trading began.
"This is America," Grasso said to a reporter. "People are free to speak their piece." Grasso conferred briefly with top police officials and then went back into the exchange building.
